title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: An employee of the Group. Distinguished for clearance: request goes to the Managing Director or, in his absence, the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Director or officer
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director (executive or otherwise) (Key Management Personnel). Distinguished for clearance: request goes to the Chair or, in his absence, the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director; distinguished for clearance, which is sought from the Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished for clearance, which is sought from the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Contractors
tiers.description: A contractor of the Group nominated by the Board from time to time as a contractor to whom this Policy applies. No distinct Approving Officer is specified for this tier.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, a parent, an unlisted body corporate which the Restricted Person controls or is a director of, a trust of which the Restricted Person is a trustee and of which he/she or a listed relative is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the Restricted Person has significant influence or control. Where the Policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act, the Restricted Person must do that act in respect of the Connected Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose an Additional Period at any time (e.g. while the Company is considering matters requiring disclosure but for the Listing Rule 3.1A carve-out). Confidential: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Company Securities is defined to include derivatives of shares (equity swaps, futures, hedges, exchange-traded or OTC options), cash- or physically-settled, with no venue limitation. 'Trade' (apply for/acquire/dispose, or agree to do so) in these requires prior written clearance at any time, and is barred in a Prohibited Period absent exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme; no clearance route is offered for this category.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: General hedging of a Restricted Person's security holding (i.e. vested shares, or shares never subject to vesting) requires prior written clearance from the Approving Officer under section 7; no separate 'vested but locked' state is described.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of securities and so a 'trade' requiring prior written clearance at any time, and is barred in a Prohibited Period absent exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or defined anywhere in the policy; only the general clearance-for-any-trade regime and a discouragement of 'short term or speculative trading' (section 9) could indirectly bear on it.
Securities lending by the Restricted Person is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named but fall within 'equity swaps ... whether settled by cash or otherwise' in the Company Securities definition, making them a 'trade' requiring prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loan agreements over Company Securities are expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer; not banned outright.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company Securities as part of a secured lending arrangement (of which a margin loan is only an example) is expressly permitted with prior written clearance; a charge or lien unconnected to any financing is not separately addressed.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: Any secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities (not limited to margin loans) is permitted for all Restricted Persons and Connected Persons, subject only to prior written clearance under section 7; no outright ban and no minimum shareholding carve-out.
rules.evidence: or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: General discouragement of short term or speculative trading; no defined holding period, LIFO basis or intention test is stated.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Restricted Persons to adopt a long term attitude to investment in Company Securities. Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

clearance.approver: Managing Director or, in his absence, the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 5 business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer.

clearance.approver: Chair or, in his absence, the Managing Director
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible (no fixed number of days stated)
clearance.evidence: Directors have agreed with the Company to provide details of changes in Company Securities they hold (directly or indirectly) to the Company Secretary as soon as reasonably possible to enable the Company to comply with its obligations under the ASX Listing Rules.

clearance.approver: Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible (no fixed number of days stated)
clearance.evidence: in case of the Managing Director, the Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible (no fixed number of days stated)
clearance.evidence: in the case of the Chair, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee

short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

exceptions.evidence: where the person is in severe financial hardship
where there are other circumstances deemed to be exceptional by the person granting the prior written clearance

A circumstance may be considered exceptional if the person in question is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, the Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for him or her to do so.

transfers of Company Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member or of Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Company Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer
a disposal of Company Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: (a) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; and (b) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade
an acquisition, or agreement to acquire, Company Securities under an employee incentive scheme

the exercise or automatic conversion of Company Securities giving a right to conversion to shares, issued under an employee incentive scheme that complies with ASIC Class Order 03/184 or 14/1000 (but not the sale of Company Securities following exercise or conversion).

financing_disclosure: all Restricted Persons: trigger is entry into a margin loan or other secured lending arrangement; disclosure is to the Approving Officer as a clearance request under section 7; deadline is before entering the arrangement (prior written clearance).

external_documents: Request for Prior Written Clearance to Trade in Company Securities (form attached to the policy)
exemption_authority: The Approving Officer for the relevant tier (Chair, Managing Director, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, or Company Secretary) may grant clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, other circumstances the Approving Officer deems exceptional, or a court order/overriding legal requirement) under section 6. Refusal terms mirror the general clearance procedure in section 7 (Approving Officer's discretion); the policy does not separately state that a refusal must be confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban secured financing outright, the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is structurally available here, subject only to obtaining prior written clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of the collar (entry, roll, unwind) needs prior written clearance regardless of whether a Blackout Period is open, so execution timing depends on Approving Officer availability and discretion on every occasion, not just around quarterly reporting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities during the periods between the end of each quarter and 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly report.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As an exploration-stage reporter, this creates four (rather than two) recurring Blackout Periods a year, narrowing the open windows available to enter, roll or unwind the collar without an exceptional-circumstances clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement... is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Blackout Period ban (though the separate 'clearance at any time' requirement in section 7 is not expressly disapplied for a forced sale, creating some ambiguity as to whether a lender can enforce without pre-clearance).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar can only be written over vested shares; no clearance route exists to hedge unvested incentive scheme interests.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the clearance or secured-lending regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (no minimum shareholding requirement is referenced anywhere in the policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no floor-based restriction that could independently block posting vested shares as collar collateral.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar appears achievable under this policy, subject to clearance at every step. Section 11 permits margin loans and 'other secured lending arrangements' over Company Securities for all Restricted Persons (and their Connected Persons), subject only to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not banned outright. The put and call fall within the broad 'Company Securities' definition (expressly including cash- or physically-settled OTC options and equity swaps) and within 'trade', so both derivative legs also require prior written clearance, needed under section 7 for every dealing at any time, not just during the quarterly Blackout Periods or an Additional Period; during those periods clearance is only available in 'exceptional circumstances' (severe hardship, other circumstances the Approving Officer deems exceptional, or a court order). Only vested shares can be used: section 10 flatly bans hedging that limits the economic risk of unvested equity-incentive entitlements. A secured lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the quarterly Blackout Period restriction. Unlike some peer policies, this one does not state that clearance refusals must be kept confidential or that they are final and unreasoned, so there is somewhat more procedural clarity, but the four-times-a-year quarterly blackout cadence narrows the open windows for execution.
